1| """Acquire for the shelves the census says are empty — the last mile, automated.
2| 
3| `mag/corpus_land.py` landed 6 books whose handles were already verified. That does not scale
4| and it cannot fill a shelf: the remaining empty shelf is east-asian (0 hits) and science fiction
5| has one file. Both need DISCOVERY, not promotion.
6| 
7| So this is the same law with a wider net, and it inherits every hard-won rule from the last
8| three days:
9| 
10|   * DISCOVER by work+author through Gutendex, never by guessing an identifier. Gutendex rate
11|     limits HARD -- measured 2026-09-29: 8 concurrent workers produced timeouts that my own
12|     fetcher turned into `{}`, and `{}` reads as "no such book". So this is SERIAL with a pause.
13|   * A timeout is never an absence. Exhausted retries return a visible `__fetch_failed__` sentinel.
14|   * VERIFY twice: Gutendex must agree with the claim, AND gutenberg.org/ebooks/<id> must return a
15|     matching title. Author disambiguates ambiguous titles -- "The Art of War" is Sun Tzu, Jomini
16|     and Machiavelli all at once, and only the author tells them apart.
17|   * GATE the download on book-likeness: >=8 KB, no HTML, Gutenberg boilerplate, >=72% letters.
18|     A 200 on a wrong path is the exact failure this project exists to catch.
19|   * Record honestly. A work Gutendex does not carry is reported as NOT-IN-CATALOGUE, never
20|     filled in from memory. "A wrong citation is worse than an honest gap."
21| 
22| Nothing is invented here. Every candidate is a real historical work named by work+author; the
23| module's only job is to find out whether Gutenberg has it, confirm it, and land it.
24| 
25| Run: python -m mag.corpus_acquire
26| """

185| def _norm(s: str) -> set[str]:
186|     return {t for t in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9']{3,}", (s or "").lower()) if t not in STOP}
187|

189| def _agree(claim: str, fetched: str) -> bool:
190|     """Do a claim and a fetched string agree? Used for BOTH titles and short author tokens.
191| 
192|     Two measured defects, and the second nearly shipped the first one back in:
193| 
194|     1. Thresholds of 5 and 6 characters meant a SHORT AUTHOR TOKEN could never agree -- `polo` vs
195|        "Polo, Marco Rusticiano" returned False, and the run was rejecting correct books.
196| 
197|     2. The first fix (a loose "one side is a subset of the other") over-corrected: it made
198|        "The Art of War" agree with "The Art of War (Jomini)", which is the exact Jomini-vs-Sunzi
199|        confusion the author token exists to prevent. The second attempt (one shared token of >=4
200|        characters) was worse still: "The Doctrine of the Mean" agreed with "The Secret Doctrine"
201|        on the shared token `doctrine` -- i.e. the Blavatsky book would have been admitted again.
202| 
203|     The lesson the two failures point at: a TITLE and an AUTHOR are different kinds of string and
204|     must not share a rule. A title is judged on how much of the CLAIM is covered, with a floor
205|     of TWO shared tokens, so one incidental shared word is never enough. An author token is short
206|     by nature and is judged on the token set being contained in the catalogue author.
207|     """
208|     c, f = _norm(claim), _norm(fetched)
209|     if not c or not f:
210|         return False
211|     if c == f:
212|         return True
213|     inter = c & f
214|     if not inter:
215|         return False
216|     # AUTHOR-style claim: short and deliberate, judged by containment in the catalogue author
217|     if len(c) <= 2 and (c <= f or f <= c):
218|         return True
219|     # TITLE-style claim: needs real coverage, never a single incidental shared word. Two shared
220|     # tokens is the floor, which is what keeps "Doctrine" from carrying The Secret Doctrine.
221|     covered = sum(1 for t in c if t in f)
222|     if covered >= 2 and covered / len(c) >= 0.6:
223|         return True
224|     return False

227| def _get(url: str, tries: int = 3, timeout: int = 30) -> tuple[int, bytes, str]:
228|     """Returns (status, body, error). Never collapses failure into an empty success.
229| 
230|     MEASURED DEFECT (2026-09-29): gutendex took 54s to answer ONE search and 36s for the same
231|     query on a second call, while the module's timeout was 30s. So most "FETCH-FAILED" rows were
232|     this seat killing a live request, and the run then died on the outer timeout before writing
233|     its receipt. A slow server is not a dead server, and a discarded result is not a negative
234|     finding.
235|     """
236|     last = (0, b"", "unattempted")
237|     for i in range(tries):
238|         try:
239|             req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA)
240|             with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
241|                 return r.status, r.read(), ""
242|         except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
243|             return e.code, b"", f"HTTP {e.code}"
244|         except Exception as e:
245|             last = (0, b"", f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:70]}")
246|             time.sleep(2.0 * (i + 1))
247|     return last

253| def _gutendex(work: str) -> dict:
254|     """Query gutendex, politely.
255| 
256|     MEASURED DEFECT (2026-09-29, round 3): gutendex started answering HTTP 503 under the round-2
257|     run's query rate, and a 503 was being recorded as a plain fetch failure -- so real books were
258|     reported as unreachable and the run moved on. 503 is a RATE signal, not a missing book, and
259|     it must be waited out with a long backoff. The gap here is deliberately larger than the
260|     per-row sleep, and the caller sees a distinct `__rate_limited__` sentinel rather than a
261|     generic failure so the receipt says "asked too fast" instead of "does not exist".
262|     """
263|     # 150s: measured 54s worst case. A shorter timeout manufactures false negatives.
264|     url = "https://gutendex.com/books?search=" + urllib.parse.quote(work)
265|     for attempt in range(4):
266|         gap = 6.0 - (time.monotonic() - _gut_last[0])
267|         if gap > 0:
268|             time.sleep(gap)
269|         _gut_last[0] = time.monotonic()
270|         st, body, err = _get(url, timeout=150, tries=1)
271|         if st == 200:
272|             break
273|         if st in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504):
274|             time.sleep(20.0 * (attempt + 1))     # rate-limited: wait it out
275|             continue
276|         return {"__fetch_failed__": err or f"HTTP {st}"}
277|     else:
278|         return {"__rate_limited__": f"gutendex returned {st} after 4 backed-off attempts"}
279|     try:
280|         return json.loads(body.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
281|     except Exception as e:
282|         return {"__fetch_failed__": f"bad json: {e}"}

83| def _get(url: str, tries: int = 3, timeout: int = 40) -> tuple[int, bytes, str]:

99| def _norm(s: str) -> set[str]:

101|     # amoeba's" while arXiv returned "Memristive model of amoeba's lattice". The titles were
102|     # IDENTICAL, and a raw-token comparison scored the apostrophe and the `&#39` as two unrelated
103|     # tokens, so a correct row was HELD. Unescaping is not cosmetic here; it is the difference
104|     # between a working gate and one that discards truth over punctuation.
105|     import html as _html
106|     s = _html.unescape(s or "")

108|             "from", "is", "are", "we", "via", "using", "towards", "toward"}
109|     # drop possessives so "amoeba's" and "amoeba" are the same token
110|     toks = {t.rstrip("'s") for t in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9']{3,}", s.lower())}

114| def _write_receipt(aid: str, meta: dict, entry: dict) -> None:

117|     The map's own rule: "fetch the PDF, sha256 it, drop a receipt under

119|     RETRIEVAL-PLAN to PULLED+HASHED." The module had NO receipt writer at all, so it could
120|     never satisfy its own rule -- 0/22 receipts existed while the ledger claimed 22 promotions.
121|     A row is only a claim until something on disk can be re-hashed against the recorded hash.
122|     """

124|     f = RECEIPTS / f"{aid.replace('/', '_')}.md"
125|     if f.is_file():
126|         return

130|         f"title: {meta.get('title', '')}\n"
131|         f"category: {meta.get('category', '')}\n"
132|         f"content_sha256_16: {entry['sha256'][:16]}\n"
133|         f"bytes: {entry['bytes']}\n"
134|         f"pulled: {datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ')}\n"

138|         f"landed: {entry.get('landed') or '(not retained)'}\n"
139|         f"\nrights_note: {entry.get('note', '')}\n"
140|         f"\nEXCERPT (verbatim, arXiv abstract, first 400 chars):\n"

155| def _arxiv_meta(aid: str) -> dict:

160|     fix. A 406 must never be recorded as a failed citation. Fall back to the plain abs page and
161|     scrape the citation_title, and only report failure if both paths fail.

166|     if st == 200:

170|         cat = re.search(r'term="([^"]+)"', t)

172|         # docs/report_v1/sources/receipts/ carries one. _arxiv_meta never returned it, so a
173|         # generated receipt would have shipped with an empty EXCERPT -- a receipt that does not
174|         # show what was actually pulled.
175|         summ = re.search(r"<summary>(.*?)</summary>", t[t.find("<entry>"):], re.S)

178|                     "licence": lic.group(1) if lic else "unstated",
179|                     "category": cat.group(1) if cat else "",
180|                     "summary": " ".join(summ.group(1).split()) if summ else "",

182|     # MEASURED DEFECT (2026-09-29, second pass): a 406 that survives the API is usually arXiv

39| def _fetch(url: str, timeout: int = 20) -> tuple[int, str]:

57| def extract() -> list[dict]:

69|         if qid is None:
70|             continue

74|         for a in ARXIV.findall(line):
75|             ids.add(("arxiv", a))
76|         for d in DOI.findall(line):
77|             ids.add(("doi", d.rstrip(".")))
78|         for u in URL.findall(line):
79|             ids.add(("url", u.rstrip(".,);")))
80|         for kind, ident in sorted(ids):
81|             rows.append({"qid": qid, "question": question, "kind": kind, "id": ident,
82|                          "asserted_in": line.strip()[:240]})

84|     seen: dict[tuple, set] = {}
85|     for r in rows:
86|         seen.setdefault((r["kind"], r["id"]), set()).add(r["qid"])
87|     out = []
88|     for (kind, ident), qids in sorted(seen.items()):
89|         out.append({"kind": kind, "id": ident, "qids": sorted(qids), "n_answers": len(qids)})
90|     return out

103|             m = re.search(r'<meta name="citation_title" content="([^"]*)"', body)
104|             rec.update(status=status, resolved_title=(m.group(1) if m else ""),
105|                        verdict="resolves" if status == 200 else f"HTTP {status}")
106|         elif it["kind"] == "doi":
107|             status, _ = _fetch(f"https://doi.org/{it['id']}", timeout=25)
108|             rec.update(status=status, resolved_title="", verdict="resolves" if status in (200, 302) else f"HTTP {status}")
109|         else:
110|             status, _ = _fetch(it["id"], timeout=15)
111|             rec.update(status=status, resolved_title="",
112|                        verdict="resolves" if status in (200, 301, 302) else f"HTTP {status}")
113|         checked.append(rec)
114|     return {
115|         "schema": "corpus_lead_verify.v1",
116|         "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
117|         "law": "a lead is promoted by title-match, never by status-match",
118|         "pack": str(PACK.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/"),
119|         "handles_claimed": len(checked),
120|         "by_kind": dict(Counter(c["kind"] for c in checked)),
121|         "resolves": sum(1 for c in checked if c["verdict"] == "resolves"),
122|         "dead": sum(1 for c in checked if c["verdict"] != "resolves"),
123|         "checks": checked,

132|         f"by kind: {v['by_kind']} · generated {v['ts']}*",

148|           "Verified wrong-handle evidence: `docs/ref/LEAD_VERIFICATION_20260928.md`."]

1| """Build the librarian's register backfill: verified real citations, ready to merge into the map.
2| 
3| `mag.librarian.py` reports 933 arXiv ids cited in cards but absent from BIBLIOGRAPHY_MAP.md, and
4| reports 220 rows that are RETRIEVAL-PLAN (source named, primary not pulled+hashed). Two very
5| different problems, and this addresses the first:
6| 
7|     907 of the 933 are CONFIRMED REAL (arXiv title fetched, control passed).
8| 
9| So the map is behind the desk on genuine literature, not on hallucination. The citation law
10| ("a wrong citation is worse than an honest gap") is satisfied by construction here: this module
11| only emits rows whose title was fetched from arXiv, so every line it produces is verifiable.
12| 
13| It does NOT touch BIBLIOGRAPHY_MAP.md. It writes a reviewable, sorted, deduplicated candidate
14| block plus a machine-readable JSON, and merging is the operator's call -- a map that silently
15| grew 900 rows on a seat's say-so would be exactly the unbidden write the standing law forbids.
16| 
17| Critically it also never marks a row PULLED: only 9 of 275 map rows are PULLED+HASHED today, and
18| conflating "the citation is real" with "we hold the paper" is the exact confusion the librarian's
19| PULLED / RETRIEVAL-PLAN vocabulary exists to prevent. Every row here lands as a PLAN, with a
20| fetched title as evidence.
21| 
22| Writes: memory/runs/corpus_gap_research/MAP_BACKFILL.md + MAP_BACKFILL.json
23| """
24| from __future__ import annotations
25| 
26| import html
27| import json
28| import re
29| from collections import Counter, defaultdict
30| from datetime import datetime, timezone
31| from pathlib import Path

38| 
39| def _theme(cited_in: str) -> str:
40|     """Bucket a citation by where it was used -- that is the only curation signal available."""
41|     p = cited_in.lower()
42|     if "moonshot" in p or "physics" in p:
43|         return "physics"
44|     if "physical_computing" in p or "cube" in p:
45|         return "physical-computing"

47|         return "self-feed"

49|         return "corpus"
50|     return "general"

52| 
53| def main() -> int:

118|     (OUT / "MAP_BACKFILL.md").write_text("\n".join(L), encoding="utf-8")
119|     print(json.dumps({k: v[k] for k in ("confirmed_real", "already_in_map", "fresh_for_map",
120|                                        "unresolved_not_claimed")}, indent=2))
121|     print("themes:", json.dumps(v["themes"]))

124|

1| """Detect NON-ANSWERS that the fan-out counted as answers.
2| 
3| `retry` reports `answered: 57/57`, but "answered" only means a row came back non-empty. B08 is
4| the proof that those are not the same thing: `or-nemotron` returned 135 words of deliberation --
5| "Not sure. ... I recall that ... Maybe I should include ... Perhaps" -- and the reasoning-strip
6| removed the scaffold, leaving a clean-looking 135-word paragraph that contains no work, no
7| author, no year and no source.
8| 
9| That row moves the headline completeness figure without moving knowledge one bit, and it is the
10| most dangerous kind of defect in this pack: it is invisible in every count I reported.
11| 
12| This module scores each answer for ANSWER-SHAPED content rather than NON-EMPTY content:
13|   * does it name a work / author / year / source at all?
14|   * how much of it is hedging rather than assertion?
15|   * how much of it is first-person deliberation?
16| 
17| A row can be non-empty, un-hedged, and still be a non-answer. So all three are scored, and the
18| verdict is the conjunction, not any single signal.
19| """

21| 
22| import json
23| import re
24| from collections import Counter
25| from datetime import datetime, timezone
26| from pathlib import Path
27| 
28| ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

31| 
32| # a citation-shaped token: an author name, a year, a source name, or an id
33| YEAR = re.compile(r"\b(1[5-9]\d{2}|20[0-2]\d)\b")

35|                     r"hathitrust|loc\.gov|doi\.org|arxiv|pg\s*#?\d)\b", re.IGNORECASE)

37| ITALIC = re.compile(r"\*[^*\n]{4,80}\*")          # a titled work
38| HEDGE = re.compile(r"\b(?:not sure|maybe|perhaps|i recall|i think|unclear|"
39|                    r"i believe|possibly|seems|might be|actually,)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
40| DELIB = re.compile(r"\b(?:i should|i don't know|i'm not|let me|as an ai|"

50|     srcs = len(set(SOURCE.findall(a)))

55|     density = (works + min(years, 5) + min(srcs, 3) + min(ids, 3)) / max(1, n / 100)
56|     # deliberation share

56|         except Exception as e:

115| def _pg_title(gid) -> tuple[int, str]:

126| def claimed_work(ctx: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
127|     """Pull (work_title, author) out of the lead's own bullet.
128| 
129|     The first version matched only `work - author` and silently dropped 44 of 70 rows, so the
130|     salvage looked catastrophic when most of those were trivially findable. Handles the three
131|     shapes the pack actually uses:
132|       * `- **Work** - Author (d. 1234) - PG 1234`   (dashes, life dates)
133|       * `- **Work**, Author, PG 1234`               (commas)
134|       * `- **Author**. *Work*. PG 1234`             (author first)
135|     Requires BOTH a work and an author, or returns None -- a half-parse is worse than a miss
136|     because it sends a nonsense title to Gutendex.
137|     """

139|     txt = re.sub(r"\bPG\s*#?\s*\d{3,6}\b", " ", txt, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
140|     txt = re.sub(r"\bGutenberg\s*#?\s*\d{3,6}\b", " ", txt, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
141|     txt = re.sub(r"https?://\S+", " ", txt)

170| def agree(claim: str, fetched: str) -> bool:
171|     """Does the fetched title plausibly BE the claimed work?

174|     the Courtier" vs "The Courtier" shares only `courtier`, and "The Art of War" vs "The Art of
175|     War" survives only if the stopword list is not eating `art`/`war`. So the rule is now
176|     SUBSET-SIGNIFICANT rather than a fixed count: every distinctive (long) token of the claim's
177|     core must appear in the fetched title, OR one rare shared token carries it.
178| 
179|     This is a promotion gate, so it stays asymmetric in the safe direction -- a loose match is
180|     still caught by the second, independent lookup against gutenberg.org in the caller.
181|     """
182|     c, f = _norm(claim), _norm(fetched)
183|     if not c or not f:
184|         return False
185|     # An exact normalised match is the strongest signal there is -- and it is the case the
186|     # distinctive-token rule silently failed, because a short title like "The Art of War"
187|     # normalises to {art, war}, every token under the 5-char floor, leaving nothing to compare.
188|     if c == f:
189|         return True
190|     inter = c & f
191|     if not inter:
192|         return False

194|     distinctive = {t for t in c if len(t) >= 5}
195|     if distinctive and distinctive <= f:

198|     return any(len(t) >= 6 for t in inter)

9|   Both failures share a cause: dedupe was done on FILENAMES, which is wrong in two directions at
10|   once. It misses a real book filed under an unexpected directory name, and it manufactures false
11|   duplicates when unrelated files reduce to the same normalized title (an earlier attempt
12|   collapsed every front-matter-less file onto one empty key and reported a false group).
13| 
14|   So: sha256 the BYTES. Two files are the same document only if they are byte-identical.
15|   Title matching is kept as a separate, advisory signal and never as a merge decision.

18|     files indexed        68,981
19|     unique hashes        62,890
20|     duplicate groups      2,308
21|     title keys              512
22| 
23|   Caveat worth stating rather than hiding: most of those 2,308 groups are NOT books. One group is
24|   a single 9-byte file replicated 825 times under corpus/oral_history/seat_pools/grok_sessions/.
25|   Real-book duplication is a far smaller number. The index reports both, because a count that
26|   mixes "the same book twice" with "the same empty marker 825 times" is not a number anyone can
27|   act on.
28| 
29| USAGE
30|     python -m mag.dedupe_index            # build/refresh and print the summary
31|     python -m mag.dedupe_index --probe F  # is F already held? (by hash, then by title)
32| """

56|     """First content-bearing line, normalized. Advisory only — never used to merge."""

61|     for line in head.splitlines()[:40]:

129| def probe(path: Path) -> tuple[bool, str]:
130|     """Is this file already held, byte-for-byte? Returns (is_duplicate, explanation).
131| 
132|     MEASURED DEFECT (2026-09-29, this session): the first implementation compared `p == path`
133|     to skip the file under test. That is a PATH identity check, and it does not work here --
134|     every caller passes a path built independently (e.g. a glob result), so the same file
135|     arrives as two different Path objects that are equal only after resolution, and on Windows
136|     the separators and drive casing differ freely. The gate therefore reported
137|     "DUPLICATE of <the file itself>" on a file that existed exactly once on disk.
138| 
139|     Verified before the fix: probing the just-landed Frontinus returned a match, and a manual
140|     sweep for that hash across corpus/ found ZERO other byte-identical copies. The gate was
141|     reporting a file as its own duplicate -- a false positive on the exact class of input it
142|     exists to judge, which is worse than no gate at all because it would make a seat delete
143|     perfectly good material as a "duplicate".
144| 
145|     The fix compares resolved paths, and -- because that is still a path comparison -- the
146|     hash is only compared against files that are genuinely a different object on disk.
147|     """
148|     path = path.resolve()
149|     digest = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
150|     size = path.stat().st_size
151|     for p in (ROOT / "corpus").rglob("*"):
152|         if not p.is_file():
153|             continue
154|         try:
155|             if p.resolve() == path:
156|                 continue
157|             if p.stat().st_size != size:
158|                 continue
159|             if hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == digest:
160|                 return True, str(p.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/")
161|         except Exception:
162|             continue
163|     return False, ""
164| 
165| 
166| def main() -> int:
167|     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
168|     ap.add_argument("--probe", type=Path)
169|     ap.add_argument("--rebuild", action="store_true")
170|     a = ap.parse_args()
171| 
172|     if a.probe:
173|         dup, where = probe(a.probe)
174|         print("DUPLICATE of " + where if dup else "NOT already held")
175|         return 0 if dup else 1
176| 
177|     print(json.dumps(build() if a.rebuild else load(), indent=2))
178|     return 0
179| 
180| 
181| if __name__ == "__main__":
182|     raise SystemExit(main())

1| """docker_ops — deterministic Docker containment probe + launch path.
2| 
3| The containerized deployment is a category-3 local op that previously only ran by
4| hand (terminal `docker compose up`). This gives it a framework path so it is
5| probed on cadence and launched/stopped via REST / CLI / queue instead of hand-run.
6| 
7| Containment = "agent subprocesses never get your full desktop." This module is the
8| measured twin of that claim: it reports the engine, validates the compose file,
9| lists containers, and flags native-process port conflicts (8765/8000/9000) that
10| would block a clean cutover.
11| 
12| Design rules (per doctrine):
13|   * Deterministic, $0, no LLM.
14|   * probe()/status() are report-only and SAFE (never mutate).
15|   * up()/down() mutate but are explicit actions (operator or a routed task).
16|   * run_cadence() only PROBES + logs to a jsonl for ghost/ops visibility. It never
17|     auto-ups or auto-downs.
18| 
19| CLI:  python -m mag.docker_ops status|probe|up|down
20| REST: GET  /api/v1/docker            (status/probe)
21|       POST /api/v1/docker {action: up|down}
22| """
23| 
24| from __future__ import annotations
25| 
26| import json
27| import subprocess
28| import sys
29| from datetime import datetime, timezone
30| from pathlib import Path
31| from typing import Any
32| 
33| ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
34| sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
35| 
36| LOG_PATH = ROOT / "logs" / "docker_ops.jsonl"
37| COMPOSE = ROOT / "docker-compose.yml"
38| # Host ports the compose file maps — these must be free of native procs for a cutover.
39| MAPPED_PORTS = (8765, 8000, 9000)
40| 
41| 
42| def _now() -> str:
43|     return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
44| 
45| 
46| def _log(event: str, **meta: Any) -> None:
47|     try:
48|         LOG_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
49|         with open(LOG_PATH, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
50|             f.write(json.dumps({"ts": _now(), "event": event, **meta}) + "\n")
51|     except Exception:
52|         pass
53| 
54| 
55| # Docker Desktop install locations (the CLI is often NOT on the interactive shell PATH —
56| # that silent PATH gap was one reason the container brain couldn't be brought up).
57| _DOCKER_BIN_PATHS = [
58|     Path(r"C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\resources\bin\docker.exe"),
59|     Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local" / "Docker" / "resources" / "bin" / "docker.exe",
60|     Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local" / "Programs" / "DockerDesktop" / "resources" / "bin" / "docker.exe",
61| ]
62| _DOCKER_DESKTOP_PATHS = [
63|     Path(r"C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"),
64|     Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local" / "Docker" / "Docker Desktop.exe",
65|     Path.home() / "AppData" / "Local" / "Programs" / "DockerDesktop" / "Docker Desktop.exe",
66| ]
67| _ENGINE_WAIT_S = 120  # how long to wait for the engine after launching Docker Desktop
68| 
69| 
70| def _docker_bin() -> str:
71|     """Resolve the docker CLI executable: PATH first, else known Docker Desktop installs."""
72|     for p in _DOCKER_BIN_PATHS:
73|         if p.is_file():
74|             return str(p)
75|     return "docker"  # fall back to PATH (works when the shell has it)
76| 
77| 
78| def engine_reachable(timeout: int = 15) -> bool:
79|     """True if the Docker engine answers `docker version` (server side reachable)."""
80|     r = _run(["version", "--format", "{{.Server.Version}}"], timeout=timeout)
81|     return bool(r.get("ok") and (r.get("out") or "").strip())
82| 
83| 
84| def ensure_engine(wait: int = _ENGINE_WAIT_S) -> dict[str, Any]:
85|     """Launch Docker Desktop if the engine is down, then wait for it to come up.
86|     Returns {ok, launched, engine_reachable, waited_s}."""
87|     import os
88|     import time
89|     if engine_reachable():
90|         return {"ok": True, "launched": False, "engine_reachable": True, "waited_s": 0}
91|     launched = False
92|     for p in _DOCKER_DESKTOP_PATHS:
93|         if p.is_file():
94|             try:
95|                 # launch detached, no window dependency on this shell
96|                 if os.name == "nt":
97|                     subprocess.Popen([str(p)], close_fds=True,
98|                                      creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0x08000000)
99|                                      | getattr(subprocess, "DETACHED_PROCESS", 0))
100|                 else:
101|                     subprocess.Popen([str(p)], close_fds=True)
102|                 launched = True
103|             except Exception as e:
104|                 _log("engine-launch-error", path=str(p), error=str(e)[:160])
105|             break
106|     waited = 0
107|     while waited < wait:
108|         if engine_reachable(timeout=8):
109|             return {"ok": True, "launched": launched, "engine_reachable": True, "waited_s": waited}
110|         time.sleep(3)
111|         waited += 3
112|     return {"ok": engine_reachable(), "launched": launched,
113|             "engine_reachable": engine_reachable(), "waited_s": waited}
114| 
115| 
116| def _run(args: list[str], cwd: Path = ROOT, timeout: int = 60) -> dict[str, Any]:
117|     """Run a docker CLI command; returns {ok, code, out, err}."""
118|     try:
119|         r = subprocess.run(
120|             [_docker_bin(), *args],
121|             cwd=str(cwd), capture_output=True, text=True,
122|             encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=timeout,
123|         )
124|         return {"ok": r.returncode == 0, "code": r.returncode,
125|                 "out": (r.stdout or "").strip(), "err": (r.stderr or "").strip()}
126|     except FileNotFoundError:
127|         return {"ok": False, "code": -1, "out": "", "err": "docker CLI not found on PATH"}
128|     except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
129|         return {"ok": False, "code": -1, "out": "", "err": f"docker {args[0]} timed out"}
130| 
131| 
132| def _native_port_conflicts() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
133|     """Which of the compose-mapped host ports are held by native (non-docker) procs."""
134|     conflicts: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
135|     # `docker ps` gives container->host mappings; anything on these ports NOT in a
136|     # running container is a native hold. We query netstat for listeners and
137|     # cross-check against container ports.
138|     try:
139|         cont_ports = set()
140|         ps = _run(["ps", "--format", "{{.Ports}}"])
141|         if ps.get("ok"):
142|             for line in ps["out"].splitlines():
143|                 for tok in line.replace(",", " ").split():
144|                     if "->" in tok:
145|                         cont_ports.add(tok.split("->")[0].rsplit(":", 1)[-1])
146|         ns = subprocess.run(["netstat", "-ano", "-p", "tcp"], capture_output=True,
147|                             text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=30)
148|         for line in (ns.stdout or "").splitlines():
149|             parts = line.split()
150|             if len(parts) >= 2 and parts[0] == "TCP" and "LISTENING" in line:
151|                 try:
152|                     port = int(parts[1].rsplit(":", 1)[-1])
153|                 except Exception:
154|                     continue
155|                 if port in MAPPED_PORTS and str(port) not in cont_ports:
156|                     pid = parts[-1] if parts[-1].isdigit() else None
157|                     conflicts.append({"port": port, "pid": pid})
158|     except Exception as e:
159|         _log("native-conflict-error", error=str(e)[:200])
160|     return conflicts
161| 
162| 
163| def probe() -> dict[str, Any]:
164|     """Deterministic report of Docker + compose + cutover readiness. Never mutates."""
165|     engine = _run(["version", "--format", "{{.Server.Version}}"])
166|     compose = _run(["compose", "config", "--quiet"])
167|     ps = _run(["ps", "-a", "--format", "{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}"])
168|     containers: list[dict[str, str]] = []
169|     if ps.get("ok"):
170|         for line in ps["out"].splitlines():
171|             parts = line.split("\t")
172|             if len(parts) == 2:
173|                 containers.append({"name": parts[0], "status": parts[1]})
174|     return {
175|         "ok": engine.get("ok"),
176|         "schema": "docker_ops.probe.v1",
177|         "ts": _now(),
178|         "engine": {"server_version": engine.get("out") or None,
179|                    "reachable": engine.get("ok"),
180|                    "error": engine.get("err") or None},
181|         "compose_file": str(COMPOSE),
182|         "compose_valid": compose.get("ok"),
183|         "compose_error": (compose.get("err") or "")[:300] if not compose.get("ok") else None,
184|         "containers": containers,
185|         "container_count": len(containers),
186|         "native_port_conflicts": _native_port_conflicts(),
187|         "cutover_ready": bool(engine.get("ok") and compose.get("ok")
188|                               and not _native_port_conflicts()),
189|     }
190| 
191| 
192| def status() -> dict[str, Any]:
193|     """Alias of probe (report-only), plus a light verdict for the dashboard."""
194|     p = probe()
195|     p["schema"] = "docker_ops.status.v1"
196|     if p["cutover_ready"]:
197|         p["verdict"] = "ready" if not p["containers"] else "running"
198|     elif not p["engine"].get("reachable"):
199|         p["verdict"] = "engine_down"
200|     elif not p["compose_valid"]:
201|         p["verdict"] = "compose_invalid"
202|     else:
203|         p["verdict"] = "port_conflict"
204|     return p
205| 
206| 
207| def up() -> dict[str, Any]:
208|     """Bring the stack up (build + start). Explicit action; not auto-called.
209|     Ensures the Docker engine is running first (self-starts Docker Desktop if needed)."""
210|     eng = ensure_engine()
211|     if not eng.get("engine_reachable"):
212|         _log("docker-up", ok=False, error="docker engine not reachable after launch attempt")
213|         return {"ok": False, "action": "up", "code": -1, "out": "", "err": "docker engine not reachable",
214|                 "engine": eng, **status()}
215|     r = _run(["compose", "up", "-d", "--build"], timeout=600)
216|     _log("docker-up", ok=r["ok"], error=r["err"][:200] if r["err"] else None)
217|     return {"ok": r["ok"], "action": "up", "code": r["code"],
218|             "out": r["out"][:500], "err": (r["err"] or "")[:300], "engine": eng, **status()}
219| 
220| 
221| def down() -> dict[str, Any]:
222|     """Tear the stack down. Explicit action; not auto-called."""
223|     r = _run(["compose", "down"], timeout=180)
224|     _log("docker-down", ok=r["ok"], error=r["err"][:200] if r["err"] else None)
225|     return {"ok": r["ok"], "action": "down", "code": r["code"],
226|             "out": r["out"][:500], "err": (r["err"] or "")[:300], **status()}
227| 
228| 
229| def run_cadence() -> dict[str, Any]:
230|     """Passive probe for the governor cadence. Report-only; NEVER up/down."""
231|     p = probe()
232|     _log("docker-probe", reachable=p["engine"].get("reachable"),
233|          containers=p["container_count"], conflicts=len(p["native_port_conflicts"]),
234|          verdict=(p["cutover_ready"] and ("running" if p["containers"] else "ready")
235|                   or "not_ready"))
236|     return p
237| 
238| 
239| def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
240|     args = argv or sys.argv[1:]
241|     cmd = (args[0] if args else "status").lower()
242|     if cmd == "up":
243|         print(json.dumps(up(), indent=2, default=str))
244|     elif cmd == "down":
245|         print(json.dumps(down(), indent=2, default=str))
246|     elif cmd == "probe":
247|         print(json.dumps(probe(), indent=2, default=str))
248|     else:
249|         print(json.dumps(status(), indent=2, default=str))
250| 
251| 
252| if __name__ == "__main__":
253|     main()

269| def _host_resolves(host: str, timeout: float = _RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_S) -> bool:
270|     """B2-107 locality law seam: can this seat NAME the host at all?
271| 
272|     One getaddrinfo, zero network bytes (resolution is not a probe). The
273|     estate already met the unresolvable-docker-name disease on the native
274|     path (models.registry.ollama_tags runs its probe on a daemon thread so
275|     an absent container hostname cannot hold a caller hostage); the doctor
276|     surface never got the same honesty until B2-107. Any resolver failure
277|     reads unresolvable: a name this seat cannot look up is not a lane.
278|     Tests monkeypatch this seam; the live trap (OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434
279|     on the host) was reproduced on real DNS before the pins landed.
280| 
281|     B2-489 hard deadline: a lookup that never ANSWERS is a second disease
282|     the first seam still carried (a 30s blackhole sleeper measured 30.1s
283|     through check_provider_endpoints, red run 2026-09-26). Windows DNS
284|     resolution is not covered by urllib timeouts, so the lookup runs on a
285|     daemon thread joined with `timeout` seconds (default _RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_S)
286|     and a lookup that does not answer in time reads unresolvable, same as
287|     NXDOMAIN; the stranded thread dies with the process, the price the
288|     registry probe already pays. The socket-level pins patch
289|     socket.getaddrinfo (tests/test_doctor_provider_endpoints.py, B2-489).
290|     """
291|     box: dict[str, bool] = {}
292| 
293|     def _lookup() -> None:
294|         try:
295|             socket.getaddrinfo(host, None)
296|             box["ok"] = True
297|         except OSError:
298|             box["ok"] = False
299| 
300|     watcher = threading.Thread(
301|         target=_lookup, name="doctor-resolve-%s" % host, daemon=True
302|     )
303|     watcher.start()
304|     watcher.join(float(timeout))
305|     return box.get("ok", False)

60| def _list_from_env(name: str, default: list[str]) -> list[str]:
61|     """Parse an allow/denylist from env var `name` as a JSON list of strings.
62| 
63|     FIX (audit finding #6, watch/inbox/MAG_SYSTEMS_DEEP_ANALYSIS_20260930):
64|     the old `":".join(default).split(":")` shredded Windows drive paths
65|     ("C:\\repo\\board" -> ["C", "\\repo\\board"]) and shredded the IPv6
66|     loopback "::1" into empty strings.  An empty deny entry matches every
67|     url ("" in url is always True -> every network_access denied while the
68|     self-test still passed) and an empty allow prefix matches every path
69|     (str.startswith("")), so malformed or empty entries fail loud here
70|     instead of silently widening or collapsing the gates.  JSON is chosen
71|     over os.pathsep because ":"-splitting shreds "C:\\..." on Windows and
72|     os.pathsep (":") shreds "::1" on POSIX; JSON keeps both intact on
73|     every surface (Windows host, WSL, Docker).
74|     """
75|     raw = os.environ.get(name)
76|     if raw is None:
77|         values = default
78|     else:
79|         try:
80|             values = json.loads(raw)
81|         except ValueError as exc:  # name the env var, not just the JSON offset
82|             raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a JSON list of strings: {exc}") from exc
83|     if (not isinstance(values, list)
84|             or not all(isinstance(v, str) and v for v in values)):
85|         raise ValueError(
86|             f"{name} must be a JSON list of non-empty strings, got: {raw!r}")
87|     return list(values)

1| #!/usr/bin/env python3
2| """falsifier_counter — measure the WATCHER's breadcrumb->action close rate.
3| 
4| Born 2026-09-05 (A2, weekend build pool). The stigmergy card
5| (watch/DEEP_SELF_STEAL_STIGMERGY_20260905.md) named the falsifier:
6| "breadcrumb -> action close rate over a week". Nobody measured it. This is
7| the measurer: a read-only pass over the breadcrumb store and the activity
8| stores, classifying each breadcrumb's lifecycle:
9| 
10|     dropped -> seen -> acted (closed) | expired
11| 
12| Breadcrumb store (dropped by mag/lane_runner.py cycle_watcher):
13|   queue/lanes/<lane>/INBOX/watcher_<stamp>.md   (+ WATCHER_CRUMB trail row)
14| 
15| Activity stores (where action would show):
16|   queue/lanes/*/trail.jsonl, state/shared_activity.jsonl,
17|   queue/room.jsonl, watch/room.jsonl, queue/handoff/*/CONVO.md,
18|   queue/lanes/*/surface.md
19| 
20| Classification (deterministic, no model calls, $0):
21|   tokens   = distinctive keywords from clue+shape+evidence (stopwords out),
22|              then RARITY-FILTERED: a token that appears in more than
23|              max(10, 0.2%) of activity rows is boilerplate (lane names,
24|              autorun ticks) and can never count — a keyword that matches
25|              everything identifies nothing.
26|   window   = --window-days (default 7) after the drop timestamp
27|   acted    = a candidate row cites the drop stamp, or matches >= N rare
28|              tokens (N=2 for row-timestamped sources: trails, shared
29|              activity, rooms; N=3 for coarse sources: CONVO/surface lines)
30|              -> status "closed", time-to-action recorded
31|   seen     = >=1 rare token match but below the acted bar
32|   open     = nothing matched, window not elapsed yet
33|   expired  = nothing matched, window elapsed
34| 
35| Honesty guards (each earned against real false positives on day one):
36|   time-travel guard — rows timestamped BEFORE the drop never count, even
37|     with every token present. CONVO.md gets PER-LINE timestamps parsed from
38|     its "[seat <ts>]" headers (unparseable lines carry the previous line's
39|     ts; the file mtime is the last resort).
40|   echo guard — trail events {WATCHER_CRUMB, SCHEDULER_UP, CYCLE} are the
41|     scheduler re-emitting the feed; they never count as action.
42|   drop-report demotion — a row that talks ABOUT the breadcrumb mechanism
43|     ("breadcrumb", "WATCHER_CRUMB") is the fleet discussing the watcher,
44|     not acting on a clue; it can raise a crumb to "seen", never "closed",
45|     unless it cites the exact drop stamp.
46| 
47| Ledger: memory/falsifier/close_rate.jsonl — append-only, typed rows
48| (row_type=breadcrumb_close | summary_close_rate), deduped on breadcrumb id:
49| a row is appended only when the id is new or its status/action changed.
50| Every breadcrumb row carries matched_by + matched_text so a human can audit
51| the machine's judgment in one line.
52| 
53| Usage:
54|   python mag/falsifier_counter.py                 # live incremental pass
55|   python mag/falsifier_counter.py --json          # machine-readable summary
56|   python mag/falsifier_counter.py --root PATH     # point at a store (tests)
57|   python mag/falsifier_counter.py --selftest      # synthetic proof, no live IO
58| """

172| def _convo_ts(header: str, year_hint: int) -> tuple[datetime | None, bool]:
173|     """Parse a CONVO bracket header like 'zcode 2026-08-26T16:32:13Z' or
174|     'zcode 09-05 ~02:5xZ'. Returns (UTC dt, dirty_minute). A dirty minute
175|     ('5x' — the ones digit unknown) means the true time lies in [M0, M9]:
176|     dt is the interval START and dirty=True. Callers matching a window must
177|     use ts_hi = dt + 9min and only count when the whole interval qualifies —
178|     an uncertain line is never smuggled across the drop boundary."""
179|     m = re.search(r"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})T(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})(?::(\d{2}))?", header)
180|     if m:
181|         try:
182|             return (datetime(int(m.group(1)[:4]), int(m.group(1)[5:7]), int(m.group(1)[8:10]),
183|                              int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4) or 0),
184|                              tzinfo=timezone.utc), False)
185|         except ValueError:
186|             return None, False
187|     m = re.search(r"(?:(\d{4})-)?(\d{2})-(\d{2})", header)
188|     if m:
189|         year = int(m.group(1)) if m.group(1) else year_hint
190|         month, day = int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
191|         try:
192|             dt = datetime(year, month, day, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
193|         except ValueError:
194|             return None, False
195|         tail = header[m.end():m.end() + 8]
196|         tm = re.search(r"[ T~]*?(\d{1,2}):(\d{0,2})x?", tail)
197|         dirty = False
198|         if tm:
199|             hh = int(tm.group(1))
200|             raw_mm = tm.group(2) or ""
201|             if len(raw_mm) == 2:
202|                 mm = int(raw_mm)                       # clean minute
203|             else:
204|                 mm = int(raw_mm or "0") * 10           # "5x" -> interval starts :50
205|                 dirty = True
206|             try:
207|                 dt = dt.replace(hour=min(hh, 23), minute=min(mm, 59))
208|             except ValueError:
209|                 dirty = False
210|         # month/day in the future of the year-hint means the previous year
211|         if dt > datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=1):
212|             try:
213|                 dt = dt.replace(year=year - 1)
214|             except ValueError:
215|                 pass
216|         return dt, dirty
217|     return None, False

41| def guarded_fetch(url):
42|     """Guard trio: https + allowlisted host + all resolved IPs global + no redirects."""
43|     from urllib.parse import urlparse
44|     p = urlparse(url)
45|     if p.scheme != "https" or p.hostname not in HOST_ALLOW:
46|         raise ValueError("host not allowed: %s" % p.hostname)
47|     import ipaddress
48|     for _fam, _typ, _proto, _canon, sa in socket.getaddrinfo(p.hostname, 443):
49|         if not ipaddress.ip_address(sa[0]).is_global:
50|             raise ValueError("non-global IP for %s" % p.hostname)
51|     class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
52|         def redirect_request(self, *a, **k):
53|             return None
54|     return urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect)

171|     """credits = ((in-cached)*in_rate + cached*cached_rate + out*out_rate) / 1000.
172|     Missing cached rate defaults to the input rate (conservative). No rates, no estimate."""

178|     cached = cached_tok or 0

180|     return round((billable_in * in_rate + cached * cached_rate + (out_tok or 0) * out_rate) / 1000.0, 9)

1| """flock_scheduler — map a batch of queued tasks onto the swarm via field-steering.
2| 
3| THE TESUJI: the swarm allocates work EMERGENTLY instead of through the serial queue.
4|   1. Each task is embedded (deterministic hash) into a shared invariant space.
5|   2. A flock field φ is built over those points (goal = solution centroid, invariants seed
6|      the penalty field from code_map.distilled()).
7|   3. Cheap agents (particles) steer: -grad(phi) pulls toward the solution, SEPARATION pushes
8|      overlapping tasks apart (the DEDUPE — replaces the central same-goal guard), ALIGNMENT
9|      keeps them on the distilled-invariants policy, COHESION clusters true duplicates.
10|   4. Each agent gets a cheapest-capable tier from one_sizer.resolve_sizing(shape, domain).
11|   5. Output: task -> agent -> (tier, model) + dedupe groups + convergence.
12| 
13| Deterministic + $0 (the field is pure; it just decides allocation before the cheap agents run).
14| Schema: flock_scheduler.v1
15| CLI: python -m mag.flock_scheduler "task1" "task2" ...  (or --demo)
16| """

33| def _embed(task: str, dim: int = 3) -> tuple:
34|     """Semantic embedding of a task into invariant space.
35| 
36|     Prefers a local Ollama semantic embedding (nomic-embed-text / all-minilm) so
37|     that distance in invariant space MEANS semantic overlap, not hash-distance.
38|     Falls back to the deterministic sha256 geometric embed when Ollama is down
39|     (never crash, but geometric = weaker clustering). This is the memlang-mindweave
40|     linchpin: RIB distance must be meaning, not hash.
41|     """
42|     try:
43|         vec = _ollama_embed(task)
44|         if vec is not None:
45|             return _normalize(vec, dim)
46|     except Exception:
47|         pass
48|     # deterministic fallback (geometric, hash-based)
49|     h = hashlib.sha256((task or "").strip().lower().encode()).digest()
50|     coords = []
51|     for i in range(dim):
52|         v = int.from_bytes(h[i * 4:i * 4 + 4], "big") / (2 ** 32) - 0.5
53|         coords.append(v * 2.0)
54|     return tuple(coords)
55|

57| def _ollama_embed(task: str, host: str = "http://localhost:11434",
58|                   model: str = "nomic-embed-text") -> list[float] | None:
59|     """Query a local Ollama embedding model for a semantic vector."""
60|     import json
61|     import urllib.request
62|     body = json.dumps({"model": model, "prompt": (task or "")[:512]}).encode("utf-8")
63|     req = urllib.request.Request(
64|         host + "/api/embeddings", data=body,
65|         headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
66|     with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=8) as r:
67|         data = json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))
68|         emb = data.get("embedding") or []
69|         if not emb:
70|             return None
71|         # truncate/pad to dim
72|         return emb[:256] if len(emb) > 256 else emb
73| 
74| 
75| def _normalize(vec: list[float], dim: int) -> tuple:
76|     """Reduce an N-dim semantic vector to `dim` dims and L2-normalize to [-1,1]."""
77|     if not vec:
78|         return tuple([0.0] * dim)
79|     # if fewer than dim, pad; else bucket-averagate down to dim
80|     if len(vec) < dim:
81|         vec = vec + [0.0] * (dim - len(vec))
82|     elif len(vec) > dim:
83|         bucket = len(vec) // dim
84|         red = []
85|         for i in range(dim):
86|             chunk = vec[i * bucket:(i + 1) * bucket] or [0.0]
87|             red.append(sum(chunk) / len(chunk))
88|         vec = red
89|     n = (sum(x * x for x in vec) ** 0.5) or 1.0
90|     return tuple((x / n) for x in vec)
91|

93| def _dist(a, b):
94|     return sum((x - y) ** 2 for x, y in zip(a, b)) ** 0.5

97| def _clusters(points: list[tuple], radius: float = 0.45) -> list[list[int]]:
98|     """Greedy single-link clustering: tasks within radius = likely duplicates (overlap work)."""
99|     groups: list[list[int]] = []
100|     assigned: set[int] = set()
101|     for i, p in enumerate(points):
102|         if i in assigned:
103|             continue
104|         g = [i]
105|         assigned.add(i)
106|         for j, q in enumerate(points):
107|             if j in assigned:
108|                 continue
109|             if _dist(p, q) < radius:
110|                 g.append(j)
111|                 assigned.add(j)
112|         groups.append(g)
113|     return groups

124|                 "learned": bool(r.get("found"))}
125|     except Exception:

129| def plan(tasks: list[str], *, domain: str = "general", sep_steps: int = 60,
130|          dup_radius: float = 0.45) -> dict[str, Any]:
131|     """Allocate a batch of tasks to the swarm: embed -> field-steer (separation = dedupe) ->
132|     cluster -> assign one_sizer tier. Returns assignments + dedupe groups."""
133|     tasks = [t for t in (tasks or []) if (t or "").strip()]
134|     if not tasks:
135|         return {"ok": True, "schema": SCHEMA, "tasks": 0, "assignments": [], "dedupe_groups": []}
136|     points = [_embed(t) for t in tasks]
137| 
138|     # DEDUPE is the key move (the tesuji): identical/near-identical tasks embed to the SAME
139|     # point in invariant space = the same work. Cluster on the ORIGINAL embedding (before any
140|     # separation), because separation is the DISPATCH force for DISTINCT agents — it must NOT
141|     # separate true duplicates (that would break dedupe). Replaces the central same-goal guard.
142|     groups = _clusters(points, radius=dup_radius)
143| 
144|     # Dedupe: keep the first task per cluster as canonical; others are duplicates.
145|     kept: set[int] = set()
146|     dedupe_groups: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
147|     for g in groups:
148|         if len(g) > 1:
149|             dedupe_groups.append({"duplicates": [tasks[i] for i in g[1:]],
150|                                   "kept": tasks[g[0]]})
151|         kept.add(g[0])
152| 
153|     # DISPATCH field (the flock): UNIQUE tasks steer apart so distinct cheap agents don't
154|     # collide when they run in parallel. Separation applies only to kept (unique) tasks.
155|     from mag import flock_field as ff
156|     uniq_idx = [i for i in range(len(tasks)) if i in kept]
157|     agents = [ff.Agent(pos=points[i]) for i in uniq_idx]
158|     for _ in range(sep_steps):
159|         for a in agents:
160|             for b in agents:
161|                 if a is b:
162|                     continue
163|                 d = _dist(a.pos, b.pos)
164|                 if 0 < d < 0.6:  # separation radius
165|                     dx = tuple((a.pos[k] - b.pos[k]) / max(d, 1e-9) for k in range(3))
166|                     a.pos = tuple(a.pos[k] + dx[k] * 0.01 for k in range(3))
167| 
168|     assignments = []
169|     for i, t in enumerate(tasks):
170|         tier = _one_sizer_tier(t, domain=domain)
171|         assignments.append({"task": t, "task_index": i,
172|                             "tier": tier["tier"], "model": tier["model"],
173|                             "shape": tier["shape"], "learned_tier": tier["learned"],
174|                             "is_duplicate": i not in kept})
175| 
176|     return {"ok": True, "schema": SCHEMA, "tasks": len(tasks),
177|             "unique_tasks": len(kept), "deduped": len(tasks) - len(kept),
178|             "assignments": assignments, "dedupe_groups": dedupe_groups}

79| def _now() -> str:
80|     return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")

83| def _seed(*parts: str) -> int:
84|     """Deterministic content-address: same (region, x, y, direction) -> same world/building."""
85|     return int(hashlib.sha256(":".join(parts).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8], 16)
86| 
87| 
88| def _watcher_line() -> str:
89|     """The Watcher/GM greeting, from the standing invariant if present (else the plain fallback)."""
90|     try:
91|         from mag import rib_bus
92|         st = rib_bus.status()
93|         ribs = (st.get("domains") or {}).get("standing-wave", {}).get("ribs")
94|         if ribs:
95|             first = sorted(ribs)[0]
96|             inv = ribs[first].get("invariant", "")[:120]
97|             return f"I am the Watcher, the standing knot of this world. {inv}"
98|     except Exception:
99|         pass
100|     return WATCHER

103| def gate(*, player: str = "you", region: str = "mycelial-republic",
104|          archetype: str = "self") -> dict[str, Any]:
105|     """THE ENTRY: the world greets you, recounts what happened while you were gone (persona_recall),
106|     and sets the scene. The vertical trigger's first beat — a player walks in and is met."""
107|     greeting = _watcher_line()
108|     recount = {}
109|     try:
110|         from mag import persona_recall
111|         recount = persona_recall.recall(archetype=archetype, region=region)
112|     except Exception as e:
113|         recount = {"ok": False, "error": str(e)[:80]}
114|     scene = (f"You stand at the edge of {region}. The world is deterministic and remembers. "
115|              f"Walk forward and a building appears where you intend to go.")
116|     return {"ok": True, "schema": SCHEMA, "ts": _now(), "player": player, "region": region,
117|             "watcher": greeting, "recount": recount.get("recount", ""),
118|             "history_n": recount.get("history", {}).get("n_events", 0),
119|             "scene": scene, "archetype": archetype,
120|             "note": "the entry: Watcher greeting + persona-recall recount + the scene (stone 1 + the gate)"}
121| 
122| 
123| def reveal(*, region: str = "mycelial-republic", x: int = 0, y: int = 0,
124|            direction: str = "forward", seed: int | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
125|     """INTENT-GATED REVEAL: 'walk forward and a building appears.' Content-addressed from
126|     (region, x, y, direction) so the SAME steer -> the SAME building (persistent fidelity). The rest
127|     of the world stays wallpaper (perceptual culling) — only the steered cell reveals."""
128|     s = _seed(region, str(x), str(y), direction) if seed is None else seed
129|     key = BUILDING_KEYS[s % len(BUILDING_KEYS)]
130|     b = BUILDINGS[key]
131|     return {"ok": True, "schema": SCHEMA, "ts": _now(), "region": region,
132|             "steer": {"x": x, "y": y, "direction": direction},
133|             "seed": s, "building": {"key": key, "name": b["name"], "line": b["line"],
134|                                     "glyph": b["glyph"], "color": b["color"]},
135|             "revealed": True, "culled": True,
136|             "note": "intent-gated: the building appears where you steered; the rest is wallpaper "
137|                     "(perceptual culling); deterministic — same steer, same building"}
138| 
139| 
140| def walk(*, player: str = "you", region: str = "mycelial-republic", x: int = 0, y: int = 0,
141|          direction: str = "forward", archetype: str = "self") -> dict[str, Any]:
142|     """The full entry beat: greet + recount (gate) + the building appears (reveal). One walk = the
143|     vertical trigger in miniature: walked in -> the world recounted -> you steered -> it responded."""
144|     g = gate(player=player, region=region, archetype=archetype)
145|     r = reveal(region=region, x=x, y=y, direction=direction)
146|     b = r["building"]
147|     return {"ok": True, "schema": SCHEMA, "ts": _now(), "player": player, "region": region,
148|             "watcher": g["watcher"], "recount": g["recount"],
149|             "scene": f"You walk {direction} and a building appears: {b['name']}. {b['line']}",
150|             "building": b, "steer": r["steer"], "seed": r["seed"],
151|             "note": "gate + reveal — the entry surface in one step"}
152|

154| def svg(*, region: str = "mycelial-republic", x: int = 4, y: int = 4,
155|         direction: str = "forward", w: int = 520, h: int = 420,
156|         step: int = 40) -> str:
157|     """BARE-METAL SVG of the revealed region (zero deps, like swarm_map): a grid of wallpaper cells,
158|     the steered cell revealed as the building, the player marker. Same steer -> same image. $0."""
159|     r = reveal(region=region, x=x, y=y, direction=direction)
160|     b = r["building"]
161|     col = b["color"]
162|     gx, gy = int(x * step) + step // 2, int(y * step) + step // 2
163|     p: list[str] = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{w}" height="{h}" '
164|                     f'viewBox="0 0 {w} {h}">',
165|                     f'<rect width="{w}" height="{h}" fill="#06070c"/>']
166|     # perceptual culling: the untouched world is low-lit wallpaper
167|     nx, ny = w // step, h // step
168|     for i in range(nx):
169|         for j in range(ny):
170|             cx, cy = i * step + step // 2, j * step + step // 2
171|             if i == x and j == y:
172|                 continue  # the revealed cell is drawn separately, lit
173|             p.append(f'<rect x="{cx - 12}" y="{cy - 12}" width="24" height="24" fill="#0c101c" '
174|                      f'stroke="#141a28" stroke-width="1"/>')
175|     # the revealed building (intent-gated): lit, labeled
176|     p.append(f'<rect x="{gx - 30}" y="{gy - 30}" width="60" height="60" rx="6" fill="{col}" '
177|              f'fill-opacity="0.18" stroke="{col}" stroke-width="2"/>')
178|     p.append(f'<text x="{gx}" y="{gy + 8}" font-family="monospace" font-size="26" fill="{col}" '
179|              f'text-anchor="middle">{b["glyph"]}</text>')
180|     p.append(f'<text x="{gx}" y="{gy + 40}" font-family="monospace" font-size="10" fill="{col}" '
181|              f'text-anchor="middle">{b["name"]}</text>')
182|     # the player marker
183|     p.append(f'<circle cx="{gx}" cy="{gy - 48}" r="5" fill="#dfe6ff"/>')
184|     p.append(f'<text x="{gx}" y="{gy - 58}" font-family="monospace" font-size="9" fill="#dfe6ff" '
185|              f'text-anchor="middle">you</text>')
186|     p.append(f'<text x="12" y="{h - 12}" font-family="monospace" font-size="10" fill="#5a6a8a">'
187|              f'region: {region} · steer ({x},{y}) {direction} · deterministic seed {r["seed"]}</text>')
188|     p.append('</svg>')
189|     return "\n".join(p)

192| def save(*, region: str = "mycelial-republic", x: int = 4, y: int = 4,
193|          direction: str = "forward") -> dict[str, Any]:
194|     """Persist the revealed region + its SVG to disk (deterministic, $0). The dashboard / a vision
195|     model can read the SVG directly. Returns the artifact paths."""
196|     OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
197|     s = _seed(region, str(x), str(y), direction)
198|     r = reveal(region=region, x=x, y=y, direction=direction)
199|     svg_txt = svg(region=region, x=x, y=y, direction=direction)
200|     svg_path = OUT / f"reveal-{region}-{x}-{y}-{s}.svg"
201|     svg_path.write_text(svg_txt, encoding="utf-8")
202|     state = {"schema": SCHEMA, "ts": _now(), "region": region, "steer": {"x": x, "y": y,
203|              "direction": direction}, "seed": s, "building": r["building"], "svg": str(svg_path)}
204|     (OUT / f"reveal-{region}-{x}-{y}-{s}.json").write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2, default=str),
205|                                                            encoding="utf-8")
206|     return {"ok": True, "schema": SCHEMA, "svg": str(svg_path),
207|             "state": str(OUT / f"reveal-{region}-{x}-{y}-{s}.json"), **state}
208|
